subject: Orbit AI — quick demo + production fit check
messages:
From: Caroline Hart <caroline.hart@orbitai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Orbit AI — demo request and production questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick product — I signed up this morning and poked around the self-serve sandbox. We did a couple of test prompts (semantic search + short generated replies) and like the latency numbers so far. Before we book a demo for the broader engineering team, can you help me understand a few production-fit questions?

Quick context: Orbit AI builds a retrieval-augmented customer support summarization product. We expect to route user queries to RAG pipelines that (1) run a short embed+search, (2) run a 512-token generate for summary/response.

Questions we want to validate in a call:
- Typical latency (p50/p95) for a 512-token generate + 64-embedding lookup on your hosted API for US region.
- Expected token cost estimates for ~500k generation tokens/day + ~50k embedding vectors/day (pilot).
- Concurrency: we're planning for up to 30 concurrent user sessions during peak; how would that map to throughput & slotting?
- Can we use a private deployment (VPC) if the pilot needs to run inside our cloud later?
- Security: do you have SOC 2 and customer-managed KMS options?

We're hoping to run a 6–8 week pilot starting mid-November and then decide on dedicated capacity. If useful, I attached a quick XLS with our guessed volume and sample API calls (pilot_requirements.xlsx).

If you can send a few short answers and a 30–40 minute demo slot for engineers+product, that'd be great.

Thanks,
Caroline Hart
Head of Integrations
Orbit AI

---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Hart <caroline.hart@orbitai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orbit AI — demo request and production questions

Hi Caroline — great to meet you and glad you got a chance to try the sandbox. Short answers up-front and then a couple quick clarifying questions so we tailor the demo to your engineering team.

Short answers:
- Latency: for a 512-token generation + a small embedding lookup in our hosted US clusters you should see p50 ~60–120ms per token after steady-state batching; p95 varies with concurrency but we generally hit 200–350ms end-to-end for similar RAG flows in our benchmarks. We can run a short perf check with your sample traffic.
- Cost: rough estimate for pilot volumes (500k gen tokens/day + 50k embeddings/day) is in the attached XLS; we include a few quantization + batching knobs that typically cut unit cost by ~30%.
- Concurrency: 30 concurrent sessions is modest — on hosted we can handle that easily with smart batching; if you need guaranteed throughput during the pilot we recommend a short Dedicated slot.
- Private deployment & KMS: yes (Private and Dedicated available). SOC 2 is available — we can share the audit pack.

A couple clarifying questions before we lock the demo agenda:
1) Typical prompt/response sizes (average tokens in prompt + expected completion tokens). You said 512 tokens for generation — is that the cap or the typical average?
2) Do you need streaming output or is full response acceptable?
3) Will the pilot include vector store calls from multiple microservices (we've seen additional tail load from many small parallel lookup requests)?

Ben (cc'd) will propose a couple of slots. If you prefer, send a Calendly link and we'll drop in a time that includes an engineer and our solutions lead.

Best,
Soogin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Caroline Hart <caroline.hart@orbitai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@orbitai.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T12:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orbit AI — demo request and production questions

Thanks — answers below inline.

> 1) Typical prompt/response sizes (average tokens in prompt + expected completion tokens).
Our prompt/embedding + retrieval stack is usually ~250 tokens before the model call; completions tend to be 150–300 tokens for human-readable summaries. Use 300 tokens average completion for planning. The 512 is a safety cap.

> 2) Do you need streaming output or is full response acceptable?
Full response is acceptable for now. We may later prefer streaming for reduced perceived latency, but not required for pilot.

> 3) Will the pilot include vector store calls from multiple microservices?
Yes — initially 2 microservices (ingest & query) in the pilot, both will make embedding calls.

I've attached the pilot_requirements.xlsx with estimated sample rates and included a short api_call_sample.txt showing the typical POST body we used against the sandbox.

Available times next week: Tue (Nov 2) afternoon PT or Thu (Nov 4) morning PT. If you can propose a 40-minute slot that includes an engineer and someone from product/solutions that'd be perfect.

—Caroline
